name: Cefazolin
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Cefazolin is excreted unchanged in the urine (70% to 80% in 24 hours). The US label keeps the usual dose down to a creatinine clearance (CrCl) of 55 mL/min, then lengthens the interval or halves the dose as CrCl falls; seizures can occur when doses are not reduced. The label gives no dialysis dosing; a literature thrice-weekly post-hemodialysis regimen and ISPD 2022 intraperitoneal doses for peritonitis are shown as non-label options.
kidney_function_basis: Label uses CrCl (mL/min; Cockcroft–Gault). Adults: adjust below 55. Children: adjust below 70.
chip: CrCl <55: longer interval or half dose

bands.recommendation: CrCl 55–59: usual dose. CrCl 35–54: usual dose every 8 hours or longer. CrCl 30–34: half the usual dose every 12 hours (label Table 5: CrCl 35–54, usual dose every 8 hours or longer; 11–34, half the usual dose every 12 hours; 10 or less, half the usual dose every 18 to 24 hours).

CrCl 11–34: half the usual dose every 12 hours (label Table 5: CrCl 35–54, usual dose every 8 hours or longer; 11–34, half the usual dose every 12 hours; 10 or less, half the usual dose every 18 to 24 hours).

CrCl 11–14: half the usual dose every 12 hours. CrCl 10 or less: half the usual dose every 18 to 24 hours (label Table 5: CrCl 35–54, usual dose every 8 hours or longer; 11–34, half the usual dose every 12 hours; 10 or less, half the usual dose every 18 to 24 hours).

hd.text: Label: no hemodialysis dosing. Literature option (not label): thrice-weekly after each session, 2 g, 2 g and 2 g, or 2 g, 2 g and 3 g (the 3 g dose after the session before the 72-hour gap may be considered for MSSA bacteremia) (Tsai 2025). These regimens are not weight-adjusted and come mostly from small pharmacokinetic studies; confirm the actual last and next session before each dose. See the site guide Antibiotic Stewardship in Hemodialysis (/guides/antibiotic-stewardship-dialysis.html).
hd.short: No label dose; lit 2/2/2–3 g post-HD

pd.text: Label: no peritoneal dialysis dosing. For PD-associated peritonitis (ISPD 2022): intraperitoneal intermittent 15 mg/kg daily (long dwell) or 20 mg/kg daily (short dwell); continuous loading dose 500 mg/L, then 125 mg/L in each exchange. Continuous cephalosporin doses may need about 25% more in patients with significant residual kidney function (ISPD 2022).

crrt.text: Not in label; the cited CRRT review (Li 2020) gives no regimen for this drug. Specialist input.
crrt.short: No CRRT data in cited sources

dialyzable: Not stated in the US label.
monitoring: CrCl for dose; seizures with excess doses in kidney impairment (label 5.2); prothrombin time in patients at risk of low prothrombin activity (label).

pediatric.approved_ages: Children for treatment indications when the needed dose matches an available formulation (DUPLEX label); perioperative prophylaxis 10 to 17 years (DUPLEX label). The alternate WG Critical Care 2 g/3 g vial label: pediatric prophylaxis not established.
pediatric.usual_dose: 25 to 50 mg/kg/day in 3 or 4 divided doses; severe infections up to 100 mg/kg/day (label, CrCl ≥70).
pediatric.max_dose: 100 mg/kg/day, not above the adult dose (label).
pediatric.notes: Label pediatric table uses CrCl (mL/min); the site band labels are eGFR.

renal.recommendation: CrCl ≥70: usual dose. CrCl 60–69: 60% of the normal daily dose, divided every 12 hours (label Table 6).
CrCl 40–70: 60% of the normal daily dose divided every 12 hours; CrCl 20–40: 25% of the normal daily dose divided every 12 hours (label Table 6).
CrCl 20–40: 25% of the normal daily dose divided every 12 hours; CrCl 5–20: 10% of the normal daily dose every 24 hours (label Table 6).
CrCl 5–20: 10% of the normal daily dose every 24 hours (label Table 6). Below 5: not stated; specialist input.

hd.text: No pediatric dialysis data in label. Specialist input.

pd.text: No pediatric dialysis dosing in label. Specialist input.

crrt.text: No pediatric CRRT data in the cited sources. Specialist input.
